What each part of a Supatype release is at, so you can tell which versions go together.

Pre-1.0: APIs and config may change between releases.

<h2 id="matrix">What a release is made of</h2>

A release is one number for the CLI and every `@supatype/*` package. The engine, server and Postgres images it runs, and the Deno that functions run on, are pinned by that release and move with it, not with the newest image on Docker Hub.

| Component | Version | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI and npm packages | `0.9.2` | The latest release, 2026-11-12. The published `@supatype/*` packages, such as `@supatype/client` and `@supatype/react`, carry the same number |
| Schema engine | `v0.11.1` | Parses the schema, plans and applies a push (`supatype/schema-engine`) |
| Server | `v2.5.2-e2e.1b79e2bc` | The Supatype server: the API, auth and the services behind it (`supatype/server`) |
| Postgres | `17.2.16` | The database image, with its extensions (`supatype/postgres`) |
| Deno | `2.9.8` | The runtime for functions and hooks |

The pins come from `release/images.json` in the repository, and the page is generated from it, so it is out of date only between a pin changing and the next site sync.

<h2 id="gap">There is no 0.4, 0.5 or 0.6</h2>

The CLI went from 0.3.6 straight to 0.7.0, on npm and as git tags. Nothing is missing from the [changelog](/changelog.html): those versions were never released.

<h2 id="check">Check what you run</h2>

`supatype --version` prints the CLI version. A self-hosted stack pins the images in its rendered compose file; `supatype self-host compose up -d` renders it again after an upgrade.
